loopIdea: The reel closes on the same early-morning driveway framing it opened on, the car easing out into the drop-off lane again, so a replay picks up the same roll-out without a seam.
mechanicTruth: Stop-and-go carpool driving turns more of the car's motion into brake heat per mile than steady highway cruising, so pads wear faster on the school run than over the same miles on the freeway; and every added passenger and backpack raises the load each tire carries, so a tire left at the same pressure flexes more and runs hotter.

storyboardBeats.narration: Stop-and-go wears brake pads faster than highway miles.

storyboardBeats.motion: Static hold as the body settles and the bulge grows

storyboardBeats.narration: Backpacks and extra kids change tire pressure, not just tread.

storyboardBeats.motion: Slow focus rack from the headlight lens back to the blade edge
